evidence: Ter. Heaut. 212: vidē sīs nē quō hinc abeās longius
Phaedr. App. 19.6: satis est, inquit, sī recēdis longius
Sen. Ep. 40.7: longius quam voluit effertur

terms.grammar: adverb; also a preposition with the accusative
evidence: Quint. 2.3.7: nec prōcēdat ultrā quam comes possit
Tac. Agr. 30.5: nūlla jam ultrā gēns
Caes. BG 1.7; Cic. Prov. Cons. 36: Gallia ulterior, Further Gaul (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: Tū, ut tempus est diēī, vidē sīs nē quō hinc abeās longius.
phrases.english: You, seeing the time of day, mind you don’t wander off any further.

phrases.latin: ut vēlōcissimus quoque, sī forte iter cum parvulō faciat, det manum et gradum suum minuat nec prōcēdat ultrā quam comes possit
phrases.english: as even the fastest walker, if he happens to be travelling with a little child, gives him his hand, shortens his stride and goes no further than his companion can

phrases.latin: satis est, inquit, sī recēdis longius
phrases.english: “it’s enough,” she said, “if you stand further back”
